correctness.rationale: Consecutive traces follow from a suffix/prefix intersection of the two endpoint inequalities. An interior block is feasible iff its two excluded flanking intervals are disjoint; the explicit interval choice establishes sufficiency. The bijection between absent blocks and nonconsecutive index edges yields each coefficient of the polynomial. Proper ordering makes components consecutive and forces exactly m-c short edges, hence the graph-intrinsic cycle-rank identity. Chordal plus claw-free forests are exactly path forests. Exhaustive endpoint matchings and seeded random checks in verify.py are corroborative, not proof.

value.rationale: For every finite proper-interval parameter graph, the theorem determines the exact number and each cardinality of possible nonalgebraic quantifier-free one-point adjacency types in arbitrary interval extensions. It isolates an intrinsic cycle-space dimension as the precise loss from maximal type capacity and classifies all maximizing bases (path forests), refining known quadratic estimates in a motivated model-theoretic neighborhood-complexity setting.
